- [x] **45. An LFO that is random: `random` and `smooth`.** *Done when:* an LFO can be given the waveform `random` (sample and hold: a number for each cycle, held until the next) or `smooth` (the same numbers, glided between) in a session file, in the
  terminal's waveform row and in the page's choice of a waveform; the engine puts out the number of the cycle it is in, and the same numbers each time a session is loaded; the page's mock engine draws the same numbers from the same hash, pinned to the engine's by a table that the engine
  writes; on the real program the LFO's bar holds one number for a whole cycle (`random`) and glides without a jump (`smooth`). *Not done:* a seed that a person can choose or a button that draws new numbers (D46, Open question 7); a random modulator that takes a new number for each note
  and not for each cycle; numbers for each voice (a modulator is lane-wide, as it was).
  - **What it was.** An LFO had four shapes, all of them a function of its phase, so that no cable could take a parameter to a number it had not been at before: a random melody on a filter's cutoff, a pan that is different for each cycle, a pitch that drifts. A modulator of that kind needs a
    number that changes from one cycle to the next, and `Modulator::tick` had none (`waveform.eval(phase)`).
  - **As built.** *Engine:* `LfoWaveform` has `Random` and `Smooth` after `Square` (indices 4 and 5, so that the index of each of the four that were there, a saved `waveform = "square"` and the protocol's order stay as they were; `ALL`, `name`, `from_str` (`random`, `s&h`, `sh`, `smooth`),
    `next` and `prev` follow the list). The number of cycle `n` of an LFO that has the seed `s` is `noise(s, n)`: the top 24 bits of `lowbias32(lowbias32(s + 0x9E3779B9) + n)` over 2^23, less 1: from -1 up to but not including 1, and exact in a 32-bit float (the seed is offset first, since the hash of 0
    is 0 and the numbers of seed 0 would have started at the bottom of the range). `LfoWaveform::eval_cycle(phase, seed, cycle)` is a shape that goes by the cycle as well as the phase: `random` is the cycle's number, `smooth` is a smoothstep from the cycle's number to the next cycle's (no corner at
    either end, so that the cycles join; a phase that is not in 0 to 1, which a negative rate in a hand-written session makes, is at the nearer end, so that it stays between its two numbers), and `eval(phase)`, which only the tests use now, is the first cycle of seed 0. `Modulator` has a `seed` and a `cycle`;
    the cycle is counted as the phase wraps (`turned as u32`: turning the rate does not start the numbers again, and a rate that goes round more than once in a buffer counts every cycle: 50 Hz at 1,024 frames is 1.07 a buffer). `AudioGraph::next_modulator_seed` gives every modulator that comes in the next seed,
    one counter for a lane's and a group's, so that a session that is loaded has the seeds in the order of its file. *Controller and protocol:* `ModulatorField::Waveform` runs from 0 to the last of `LfoWaveform::ALL` (derived, `(0, 5)`), the protocol's `Waveform` has the two names, and the generated `Waveform.ts`, `WAVEFORMS` and
    the range are regenerated; the loader, the saver (`waveform.name()`), the tree's label (`LFO 4.0Hz random`), the intents and the client's reducer needed nothing else, since they go by the list. *Terminal:* the waveform row of an LFO is built from `LfoWaveform::ALL`, so `Left` and `Right` go round six.

- [x] **49. The tempo (an extra, the first of the patterns' parity).** *Done when:* the tempo that patterns are recorded at is the session's, which a session file can say (`bpm`), which the terminal's `b` and the page's field set by the one intent, `SetBpm`, so that it is a step of the history, marks the session changed and is told to every front-end as an event; a pattern that has been recorded keeps the tempo it was recorded at; and on the real program a tempo typed into the page's field is the engine's, a second page's, the saved file's, and is put back by one Undo. *Not done:* the patterns themselves in the page (recording, clearing, their settings: the next steps), a pattern that follows the tempo (Open question 10), a metronome or a tap tempo.
  - **What it was.** The tempo was the controller's (`global_bpm`), worked out from the first recorded pattern when the controller was made; the model, which is what a save writes, had none.   - **The laws** (`CLAUDE.md`, "MIDI-learn modulator"). A velocity is the velocity of the last note-on the lane plays over 127, unipolar as a CC (`base + velocity * depth * range`), at rest (0) before a note, and it keeps its value when the note ends (a release goes by its own note's
    velocity); a note-on with no velocity is a note-off, and a note-off that has a velocity (64 on many keyboards) is not a note. A key is the number of the last note over 127 and is bipolar around middle C: `base + clamp((note - 60) / 60, -1, 1) * depth * range`, so that note 60
    adds nothing and five octaves either way are the whole of the depth; it rests at note 60. - [x] **53. Mute and solo (an extra: silence a lane or a group, or hear only one).** *Done when:* a lane or a group can be muted and soloed from a session file (`mute`, `solo`), from the terminal (`M` and `S` on the chain) and from the page (a cell on its node);

  - **What it was.** The only way to hear one part of a session was to turn the volumes of the others down, which loses the numbers a person had set, or to take a node out. A volume is the user's number and a mute is a state, so it is a flag of its own.
  - **The laws** (`CLAUDE.md`, "Mute and solo"). A muted lane or group is never heard, and a mute wins over a solo (a lane that is muted and soloed is silent, and being soloed it silences what is not soloed all the same). While anything, a lane or a group, is soloed,
    only what is soloed is heard: a soloed lane, a lane in a soloed group, and a group that is soloed or has a soloed lane in it (its bus is heard for that lane, with its volume and effects, and its other members are not). A lane's mute is its own: a lane in a
    muted group is not muted itself (its meter reads) and the bus is cut. The audio thread lets a lane go, or brings it back, after its volume and its effects and before its meter, and a bus after its effects, by a linear ramp of its gain over the buffer (`fade`,
    5.3 ms at 256 frames); a gain that is 1 and stays so costs nothing, and one that is 0 and stays so puts zeros and multiplies by none, so that a plugin that puts out `NaN` is silenced by a mute. The scope taps of a node are before it (they show the signal of the
    node), the meters after.
  - **As built, in five commits.**
    - *The engine and the file* (`b832da3`): `GraphCommand::SetMute`, `SetSolo`, `SetGroupMute` and `SetGroupSolo`; the flags of a lane and of a group in the audio thread, with the gain they were heard at when the last buffer ended (`heard_at`); `fade`; the file's
      `mute` and `solo`, written only when on; the model's flags, the loader that sends what a file turns on and the saver; 18 tests.
    - *The intents, the history and the client layer* (`a40ee03`): `Intent::SetMute` and `SetSolo`, `Event::MuteSet` and `SoloSet`, the controller's `set_mute` and `set_solo` (refused for a node that is neither a lane nor a group), a step of the history for each (the words above, no
      key), the snapshot's and the graph's flags (`NodeKind::Instrument` and `Group` have `muted` and `solo`), the put-back of a lane and of a group, which carry them, the regenerated types and fixtures, the page's reducers, `Editor.setMute` and `setSolo`, and the mock
      engine's values and history.
    - *The terminal* (`4ca9667`): `M` and `S` on the Session tab's chain (the lane or the group the selected entry is of: a group's header, bus effect and modulator are the group's), a `[mute]` and a `[solo]` after the name in the tree, the two keys in the action bar of an
      instrument and of a group (their neighbours' labels shortened to fit 120 columns), the Help text, and the golden snapshots.

    the note before (the spec's `heard` and `silent` wait for the quiet, and it passed 12 runs of 12 after that, and the mutants that break the engine's law are caught by it). - [x] **63. A drive (an extra): four shapes made at twice the rate, a tone and a level, and a wavefolder to try it with.** *Done when:* there is a built-in effect, `builtin:drive`, that every front-end lists (the terminal's selector, the page's "fx" menu, a session file by its id, `tang enumerate`), with a choice of four shapes (soft, hard, tube, fold), a gain into them, a tone, a level and four presets; a sound with no drive is the sound that went in (late by the oversampling's delay), a fold goes back on itself where a hard shape stops, what a shape makes above the Nyquist frequency does for the most part not fold down into the band, and each of these is held by a test; and `examples/fold.toml` puts the fold to use with a slow LFO on the drive.
  *Not done:* anti-aliasing beyond the doubled rate (the hard shape and the fold still alias at the top of the knob, -25 dB for a sine through the hard shape: antiderivative anti-aliasing is the way on, at the price of a half-sample of delay and a mild low-pass in the straight part of the curve), other shapes (a bit crusher, a rectifier, a tape curve), a delay that the host makes up for (it has no way to be told: a drive is put in fully wet), and a drive as a stage of the oscillator's own.
  - **What it was.** The built-ins were an oscillator, a filter, a delay and a reverb: a sound could be shaped by a filter and echoed, but not bent, and a modulator had no parameter that changes the colour of a sound as much as the gain into a shape does (an LFO on a drive is the sweep that analog synths are known for, and on a fold the one that West-coast synths have).
  - **The plugin** (`CLAUDE.md`, "Built-in plugins"; `src/plugin/builtin/drive.rs`). `type` (soft, hard, tube, fold), `drive` (0 to 1, a gain of 0 to 36 dB, the knob linear in decibels), `tone` (a one-pole low-pass, exponential from 500 Hz to 20 kHz, none at the top) and `level`; the four presets are Warm, Crunch, Fuzz and Wavefolder, level-matched to each other (each 1.32 to 1.42 times as loud as a sine of 0.25 that goes in, 2.4 to 3 dB over it). The shape is made at twice the rate by a half-band filter of 47 taps up and another down (`half_band_taps`, a Kaiser window on the ideal filter), at a delay of 23 frames. Measured: the filter is 6.02 dB down at the input's Nyquist frequency, 45.6 dB at 28 kHz and past 76 dB from 30 kHz, and flat to 16 kHz within 0.1 dB; a sine of 3137 Hz through the hard shape at the top of the knob has 0.3% of its power in no harmonic (-25.3 dB; 3.2%, -15 dB, when the shape is made with no oversampling), and 0.0045% (-43.5 dB) at half of the knob; the soft shape and the tube are at -28.5 and -47 dB, the fold at half of the knob at -33.8.

- [x] **70. P0 of the patch graph, the oracle and the boundary (an extra; `docs/patch-graph.md` §11.6): what the engine renders, held, so that a new engine can be held to it.** *Done when:* the audio callback renders with an engine behind a trait (`audio::Engine`, which `AudioGraph` implements); `src/oracle/` renders a corpus (20 sessions, and 300 that a seeded generator makes, each with a script of notes and controllers, the generated ones also with edits made through the controller while they sound) through the callback's own `Renderer` at 64, 256 and 1024 frames, and holds every render to what it was: to the bit, by a hash, for the platform it was made on, and to 1%, by numbers, for every other; the engine renders the same bits twice; no block that takes no command asks the allocator for memory; two engines can be run on one scenario and compared bit for bit; and a benchmark says how long a block takes against the time it has.

  *Not done:* P1, the kernel (the next step of §11.6; done in step 71); a recording of a pattern among the edits (a recording is four beats of metronome before it records, so that a scenario would be two seconds longer for it); exact hashes for Linux and Windows (their CI is held to the numbers, which I have not been able to run: see the limits); sessions that name a plugin that has to be installed (CLAP, VST3, LV2); and listening, which is yours (see the limits).

  - **What it was.** The risk of a new engine is that it is not the old one (§11.6), and the old one was held by 1,911 tests of its parts and, as a whole, by the twelve examples' tests (a chord that is heard, measured within a tolerance): nothing could say that two engines are the same, and a few of its properties were taken for granted (that a render is the same every time; that the audio thread does not allocate). You asked for the best way to a truly modular system that is still fast, I answered with a compiled graph kernel reached by growing it under today's structure with the old engine as the oracle (`docs/patch-graph.md` §11), and you said go (*"lets go e2! I like this. I like it all!"*), which takes the six recommendations of its §11.7 as the plan (E2 by the path of §11.6, the netlist as the file's form with today's sugar kept, a richer event with note ids, polyphony inside `Patch` nodes, the cores built last, the kernel in a crate of its own, our own kernel and not a library). P0 is the first of the eight steps there. It changes nothing that a person hears except what its three findings fix.
  - **What it is.** *The boundary* (`b9d347d`): `audio::Engine`, the trait that the callback's `Renderer` renders with (`num_channels` and `process(midi, out)`), implemented by `AudioGraph` and by `Box<dyn Engine>`; `Renderer::new` and `AudioEngine::build` take any engine. *The rig* (`src/oracle/mod.rs`): a `Scenario` is a session as text, a script of `(frame, bytes)` notes and controllers (frames, not blocks, so that it is the same notes at every block size), edits, a block size and a rate; a `Rig` loads it as the program does (`load_session`), puts a `Controller` round it over stub channels (with the program's own bounded channels for what the engine reports, and the built-in catalog), and drives it a block at a time through `Renderer`: the edits that have their frame in the block are made, the notes are sent at their place in it, the block is rendered (timed, and the allocator's calls counted: `alloc_guard`) and `poll()` lets the controller see what the engine reported. `render` is all of a scenario: the samples, a hash of all 4,096 telemetry cells after every block, the allocations of each block and what became of the edits; `fingerprint` boils it down to two hashes and the peak, the rms and the rms of each eighth; `agree(scenario, make_a, make_b)` renders it with two engines and names the first sample that differs (its frame, block and channel), or the first block whose telemetry does; `legacy` makes the `AudioGraph`, from the `Wiring` (the channels and cells that an engine is built from). *The corpus:* `src/oracle/sessions/` (the fifteen examples and the tracer scene as they were, copies, and four that the generator does not draw: `cross`, a group's modulator that drives a member's modulator and the depth of one of its cables; `mix`, a muted group, a muted lane; `solo`, a soloed lane in a group; `remap`, a note remap with a pitch bend range, a velocity, a key and a macro control and a pattern that is in key), all played with a chord, the wheel up and back, the pedal, a key hit while the pedal is down, all sound off; and `oracle::generate`: 300 sessions from a seed (xorshift64*, a generator of our own, the same on every platform: one to four lanes of the oscillator, up to two groups, effects of the four built-in kinds with parameters drawn from what the plugin says it has, every kind of modulator (LFOs of every shape with sync, retrigger and fade; envelopes; macros; step sequencers; MIDI controls of every kind, some unbound to learn) with cables to the plugins of the lane, to a group's members and bus, and between modulators, mutes, solos, ranges, transposes, remaps, patterns), with a script (two to five notes, some of them on the member channels of an MPE controller with their own wheel and pressure; controllers; the sustain pedal; a key that is hit again; all notes off and all sound off) and edits. 50 features of the sessions are counted by a test that says how many of the 300 must have each.
  - **Edits** (`oracle::edits`). What a front-end asks of the controller while the session sounds, which a file cannot show (a fade is made when a mute *changes*): `Edit` is a request in terms that mean something in every session (a parameter, a mix, a volume or a pan; mute and solo of a lane or a group; an effect added, moved or taken out, of a lane or a bus; a modulator added, or made for a parameter with its cable; a range; a lane put in a group; a lane or a group added or taken out; a preset; the tempo; Undo and Redo): the lane is a place among the lanes and wraps round the lanes there are when the edit is made, so that it aims at something whatever has gone before. `resolve` makes the intent that a front-end would send, from the model as it is; one with nothing to aim at is skipped; one that the controller refuses is counted as refused; the rest go through `Controller::apply` as the terminal's and the browser's do, so they are in the history. The generated sessions have four to ten of them each, at frames from a twelfth to the most of the way through.

An output that has a cable and the chain link has two cables leaving it, so the chain link is a sum of one there (the kernel's rule for a `single` input, which is the only change to what a lane with a cable makes: the sign of a zero). the page's `audibleOf`, `ownAudibleOf`, `heardOf` and `fedOf` are the law written again, pinned to a run of the engine over every combination of the mutes and solos of two groups and four lanes that have five cables between them (4,096 cases: the lane's own sound, its chain and each bus, `fixtures/audibleCables.json`), and a lane that is heard only for what it is sent has its instrument dimmed and its effects not; the mock engine's meters follow the law (a group that is heard for a cable reads, and one whose lanes have their way out cut does not); `examples/shared-reverb.toml` with the saw soloed is the session with the square muted, to the bit; and a browser spec soloes a lane that has no way out and hears it through the filter of a lane that is not soloed, on the real program.

  *Not done:* soloing what only cables feed does not let in what feeds it (the room of `examples/shared-reverb.toml`, soloed alone, is silent: the law goes one way, from what is soloed to what it sends to; a console lets the sends of what is not soloed feed a soloed return); the mock engine's master meter and scope still hear every lane that has an instrument, is let in by the solo and is not muted, whatever its way out and the ends of its cables (it reads a level for a session whose lanes all have no way out, which the engine does not); the terminal still does not show cables (P3e).

  - **What it was.** Step 77 left it open on purpose: a lane's tail was gated by what the lane is heard for, so that a lane that is not soloed while something is, with a cable to a reverb on another lane, was as silent as before, and what a soloed lane sent into a lane that is cut by the solo was lost in that lane's tail.
  - **What it is.** *The engine* (`src/plugin/chain/nodes.rs`, `chain.rs`). `Schedule::set_gates(lanes, groups)` is called by `AudioGraph::process` after `refresh` (it finds the owner of each end of a cable by the plan's places: `Owner`, `owner_of`, `Cable::{from_owner, to_owner}`) and before the plan runs. A lane has `solo_heard` (let in by the solo: nothing is soloed, or it is, or its group is), `live` (heard for what is sent to it), `receives` (a cable that is not told to go ends in its chain), and the head gate `head_at` / `head_goal`; a group has `solo_heard` and `live`; `own()` is `!muted && solo_heard` and `out()` is `!muted && (solo_heard || live)`. The liveness goes through the cables again until nothing changes (a lane's or a group's flag is only set, never taken back, in a pass, and the cables go one way, so `cables + 1` passes are the most), then a lane that is live and whose way out is not cut lets its group in in the same pass. The goals are then: `heard_goal` is `out()` (the lane's tail and the group's bus), the head gate is 0 for a lane that receives and is not let in by the solo and 1 for any other, and a cable's goal is its level by the gate of its start (a mute is `!muted` in both). *The head gate* is applied in `run_head` after the scope tap (the node's scope shows what the instrument plays, as it does under a mute), as one ramp over the buffer, `fade(out, channels, from, to)`: at once to its goal while the lane's tail was not heard at the end of the last buffer (`heard_at == 0`), and held where it was while the tail is to go down in this one (`heard_goal == 0`), so that the ramp of the gate and the ramp of the tail, going opposite ways, do not let through the product of the two (a bump of the lane's own sound, 25% at the most, for the buffer in which a cable is drawn into a lane that is not heard or taken out of one). *Nothing is allocated* (`a_session_with_a_solo_and_cables_asks_the_allocator_for_nothing_once_it_is_running`, the oracle's `no_block_after_the_first_asks_the_allocator_for_memory` on the whole corpus), and a session that has no solo, or no lane that cables end in, has a gate of 1 everywhere and the bits it had. *The oracle.* `SOLO_EDITS` (12 edits on the session `CABLED`: two cables drawn between a lane in the group and a lane outside it, a solo on each of them one after the other, a mute, a group that is soloed, a lane that is taken out while it is soloed and put back by Undo, the solos taken off) is the scenario `edited:solos` (three renders, 978 in all, 50 of them always on) and a test reads the sound in two windows: with the solo on lane 1 the reverb on the bus of the group is heard for its send, and with it on lane 0 lane 1 is heard for what lane 0 sends it, which without the cables is nothing. *The page* (`web/src/client/audible.ts`). `lawOf` is the law as the engine has it (`own` for what a lane is heard for by itself, `out` for what its chain or a group's bus is heard at, `fed` for what a cable from something that is heard puts sound into), found by the same going through the cables; `heardOf` is `out`, `audibleOf` is what reaches the master (`out` and the bus of the lane heard), `ownAudibleOf` is what a lane's own sound reaches it by (a lane's instrument node; for a group it is `audibleOf`), `fedOf` is `fed`; `audibleAt` (`client/selectors.ts`) is `ownAudibleOf` for an instrument, `audibleOf` for a group and for the effects in a lane's chain, so that a lane that is heard only for a send is drawn with its instrument dimmed and its effects not. *The mock engine* (`MockServer.frame`): a lane reads for `heardOf`; a group reads when it is heard and a cable from something that is heard feeds it (`fedOf`) or a lane in it is heard whose way out is not cut (it read for any lane that was heard, whatever its way out: step 77 left that). *The example.* `examples/shared-reverb.toml` says in its header what soloing an oscillator does, and a test holds it: with the saw soloed the session is the session with the square muted, to the bit, the room being heard for the saw's cable though nothing in its group is soloed.
  - **The held things.** *Rust* (20 tests that are new, in the files named, and one that was changed, the engine's random wirings): the engine (`chain.rs`, 17 in the section "the law of mute and solo for what a cable carries": a lane that is soloed is heard through the effect of a lane that it sends to, which puts out only what it is sent; the lane's own sound is let go of over a buffer by the head gate, exactly (`1.5 + 0.5 h`), and comes back over one; a soloed lane that is muted sends nothing, and neither does a cable that is at nothing; a lane that is muted is not heard for what is sent to it; what a lane is sent goes on through the cables of its effects to the lanes after it; a lane that is soloed is heard through a bus effect of a group that has no lane soloed, and the group is heard for it; a group is heard for a lane in it that is heard for what it is sent and for nothing else of what is in it; a lane is heard for what a group that is soloed sends to it; a lane that goes nowhere by itself is heard through its own cable; no allocation; a bus and a chain that make a sound of their own, which is what can say whether a group or a lane is heard (a scaling effect puts out nothing for nothing); what a lane that a cable let in is let go of by, over the same buffer as the cable, with none of its own sound in it; none of the sound of a lane that the solo does not let in is heard over the buffer in which a cable comes in; what a lane sends by the cable of its instrument goes with its own gate; and a lane that is heard only for a send lets in nothing by the cable of its instrument), the engine's random wirings (400 of them, now with solos of lanes and of groups from a stream of their own, so that the wirings that the other draws make are the ones they were: every sound is checked against `RandomWiring::value`, the law written as the recursion that it says, where a lane that only its own effect's cable would let in is not let in; measured over the 400, 44 have a lane that is heard only for a send and 29 a group), the plan (`nodes.rs`: two tests call `set_gates`), the oracle (the scenario, and the test of its two windows), the fixture (`the_web_clients_fixture_of_what_is_heard_with_cables_is_current`, which writes `fixtures/audibleCables.json`: 42 KB, 4,096 cases, 57 different results, 254 cases in which a lane's chain is heard and its own sound is not and 934 in which the bus of the second group is heard for a cable and its lane is neither heard for itself nor for a send) and the example (above). *The pure parts and the components* (vitest): `audibleCables.test.ts` (11: all 4,096 cases of the engine for what a lane is heard for, its chain and each bus; that the fixture is not a thin one; that a session with no cable is what it was; a lane that a soloed lane sends to is heard through its chain and not for itself; a cable at nothing or from a lane that is muted carries nothing; chains and the output of a group and the effects of a bus; a group is heard for a lane that is, and not when its way out is cut; `fedOf`; that it is worked out once for a graph), `selectors.test.ts` (`audibleAt` with cables: nothing soloed, the lane that is sent to and its group, the effect that a group's output goes to) and `connection.test.ts` (the mock engine's meters: a group that a soloed lane sends to reads and its lanes do not, a lane that is sent to reads and so does its group, a lane that is muted sends nothing, a group does not read for a lane whose way out is cut). *The browser* (`e2e/solocables.spec.ts`, two): on the mock engine a lane is soloed that has a cable to the filter of the other, and its instrument is dimmed and the filter not, until the cable has no level (the filter is dimmed), the sender is muted (everything is dimmed) or the other lane is soloed; and on the real program the way out of the second lane is cut, so that what it plays can only reach the master through its cable into the first lane's filter, and with it soloed it is heard (14 s) and the first lane's own notes are not, a muted lane lets go of what it is sent, a lane that is muted and soloed is not heard, the cable taken out is silence, and undo has it back.
  - **Decisions I made, which you may overrule** (D78). That the solo goes one way, from what is soloed to what it sends to, and not back to what feeds it: soloing the room of `examples/shared-reverb.toml` alone is silent, as nothing that is heard sends to it (a console would let the sends feed a soloed return); the other way is a flag on a lane that lets its sends through, or a solo that lets in what feeds what is soloed for its sends only, and wants a decision of its own. That a lane that is heard only for what it is sent has none of its own sound, in its chain or in the cable of its instrument, and what is sent through the cables of its effects goes on (an instrument that sends to another lane's effect lets that lane in only if it is let in itself): a lane that is let in for a send is a place that the sound passes, not a voice. That a mute is not a head gate (a lane that is muted and let in goes on, and its tail cuts it, as a mute always did), and takes the cables of the lane with it. That a group is heard for a lane in it that is heard for a send only if the lane's way out is not cut (a lane that goes nowhere puts nothing into its group). That the least set is the law: what only a cable from its own effect would let in is not let in. That what a lane's effects hold of its own sound (a reverb's tail, a delay's repeats) is heard when the lane is let in for a send, as it is when a mute is let go (the head gate shuts what comes in and not what the effects hold; `Plugin` has no reset). That the head gate is a ramp over the buffer like the other gates and not at once, except when the lane is not heard or is let go of, where a ramp would only let through a bump. That the page dims a lane's instrument while its effects are not dimmed, and has no third state.
  - **As built, in 4 commits.** The engine, the oracle and the fixture (`571ee64`), the page's law, `audibleAt`, the mock engine's meters, their tests and the browser spec (`02e2e8b`), the example's test and header (`22d4ab9`), and the docs (this entry, D78, what is built in §11.6, and `CLAUDE.md`).

The engine's going through the cables again until nothing changes finds the least set, which is what the law says; the evaluator goes by paths now. *A bump of a lane's own sound, found by a mutant that survived:* a cable that is drawn into a lane that is not heard, or taken out of one that is let go of, made the head gate and the lane's tail go opposite ways over one buffer, and the lane's own sound that the solo does not let in came through as the product of the two ramps (at most a quarter of it, for 5 ms); the mutants "a cable that is told to go is a cable that lets in" and "a cable that is told to go sends" both survived the engine's tests, and the exact ramps that now hold it are among the new tests. *What cannot be seen through a scaling effect:* the tests of the law that put a doubling effect in a lane or on a bus could not tell a group that was heard from one that was not, since what is scaled is nothing; three mutants survived for it, and the tests that hold the law now have an effect that adds a constant. *The mock engine's group meters* read for any lane that was heard, whatever its way out (step 77 left it): a group read when its only lane had no way out. *Equivalent mutants:* of the engine's 62, seven are no fault: a muted group or lane that what is sent to it lets in is not heard all the same (`out` has the mute), a lane that is heard for itself has its group let in by the solo already, a cable that starts at a node that is not in the plan sends nothing and is let through at nothing (the plan's places make it silence: a state that nothing reaches), a head gate that a mute shuts when the lane's tail is shut already, and a cable that is told to go and ends in a lane that is let go of (the gate is held while it is let go of); of the page's 46, two are no fault (a cable that starts at the master is nobody's; a group is a bus too, and has no parent) and two were removed with the code that they were in (`ownerOf` of an instrument, which no cable ends at, and what `audibleAt` asked for a group, which `ownAudibleOf` says as `audibleOf` does).

  - **What it was.** The × of a lane on the page took out the whole lane (`RemoveNode` of the lane: its instrument, its effects, its modulators and its pattern; the menu said "its 4 effects and 2 modulators go with it"). The terminal's `d` took out the instrument alone (a second `d` the lane), but by a method of the controller that no intent asks for (`Controller::clear_instrument`), which forgets the history: the page could not ask for it and Undo could not put the instrument back. And the engine did not run the effects of a lane that had no instrument (`Lane::run_fx` returned at once: "nothing to work on", which was true before there were cables): effects that stayed in such a lane would have been on the canvas and silent, with a cable from another lane into them too.
  - **What it is.** *The intent.* `ClearInstrument { node }` (`Intent`, `apply.rs`: `clear_instrument_intent`, told as a snapshot): `Controller::clear_instrument` takes out the cables that drove the plugin (a lane's and a group's, each written down as a cable), asks the audio thread to hand the plugin to a channel of its own and writes down `Inverse::Instrument` (the model's plugin, the note remap and the pitch bend range, what keeps the plugin: the same record as for an instrument that is replaced, `Replaced`), empties the lane's slot in the model and forgets its remap. The step is `Plan::Removed` in the words `take Oscillator out of its lane`; undo gets the plugin (loaded again from the model if it was not handed back), swaps it back in, and puts the cables back after it; redo takes it out again. Refused, with nothing changed and no step, for a node that is no lane (`an instrument is taken out of a lane`) and for a lane that has none (`the lane has no instrument to take out`). *The engine.* `GraphCommand::ClearInstrument { inst, keep }` (`hand_back`, as for `SwapInstrument`), and `Lane::run_fx` (`nodes.rs`) runs the effects of a lane whether or not it has an instrument. *The terminal.* `d` on an instrument that has a plugin asks the intent (a step now), and on a lane that has none the removal of the lane, as before. *The page.* The × of a lane that has an instrument opens "Keep …", "Remove … only: its N effects and M modulators stay in the lane" and "Remove the lane … for good: …"; the lane stays on the canvas as `(empty)`; the focus goes to the button that puts an instrument in. `Editor.clearInstrument`, `Removal.instrument`, the mock engine's `clearInstrumentOutcome`, and the history's step. *The oracle.* `Edit::ClearInstrument { lane }` and the scenario `edited:instruments` (it has a cable, so the loop that the plan replaced, which stops the effects of a lane that has no instrument, is not held to it).
  - **The held things.** *Rust* (tests of the engine, the controller, the intent, the history, the terminal and the oracle): the effects of a lane that has no instrument run, on silence and on what another lane sends to them; the effects go on running when the instrument is cleared; a plugin that is cleared goes to the channel that asked for it and else the usual way (no channel, nobody listening, a full channel); a lane that has none hands nothing back; the intent takes the instrument out, the cables to it and leaves the rest, and refuses what it must (every node kind); every instrument of a session that has a note remap, a group's cable and the lane's own is put back by undo as the very plugin with its cables and remap, and taken out again by redo; the order of the commands; the plugin that was not handed back is loaded again; a lane that is gone refuses the undo with the reason and the step is dropped; the TUI's `d` is the intent (the commands, the step, Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y), and a second `d` takes the lane; the edit is skipped for a lane that has none and its scenario is heard (the lane that has no instrument is heard through its delay for what a cable sends it: an rms of 0.0328 of the difference, and exactly 0 where the effects do not run). Five scripts of `history.json` pin the mock engine to the controller. *The page:* the menu's items for every kind of lane and group (words and grammar of what stays), the only lane, the empty lane, a press asks the intent and the lane is on the canvas as `(empty)` with its effect and modulators, Undo and Redo through the app, the focus, a refusal.
  - **Decisions I made, which you may overrule** (D85). That the lane stays when its instrument goes: a lane is what an effect chain hangs from (effects are not nodes of their own yet: P5 and P6), so the page shows an `(empty)` node, which holds the lane's keys, group, mute, solo, way out and pattern, in place of the oscillator. That the effects of a lane that has no instrument **run always**, and not only when a cable ends at them: the rule is the simplest, the cost is the effects' work on silence, and the corpus has no lane without an instrument, so that the 52 renders that were held to the bit are the same bits (and the whole corpus is the same under the plan and under the loop). That the only lane of a session has a × now (it can have its instrument taken out). That the terminal's `d` is the intent (a step), where the method forgot the history.   - **What it was.** A cable from a modulator named what it drove by a place: a slot in a lane's chain, a member's ordinal in a group, the index of a bus effect or of a sibling modulator, a cable's place in its modulator (`ModTargetKind`). A place is true only until something comes or goes, so the model had 20 functions (`shift_*` after an insert, `fixup_*` after a remove, `remap_*` after a move: 304 lines of `model.rs`) that renumbered every cable of every rack at every change of structure, mirrored by 31 functions of `chain.rs` (443 lines) on the audio thread, and the history had to tell the cables the places they had *now* before anything went in. And the audio thread had every command that addresses a rack twice, once for a lane's and once for a group's: ten pairs (`InsertModulator` and `InsertGroupModulator`, `RemoveModulator`, `AddModTarget`, `InsertModTarget`, `RemoveModTarget`, `SetModTargetDepth`, `SetModulatorRate`, `SetModulatorWaveform`, `SetModulatorSource`, `SetModulatorEnvelopeParam` and their group's), which a third kind of rack would have made thirty.

A free modulator reaches any parameter of any plugin of the session (the instrument of a lane that has one, an effect of a lane's chain, an effect of a group's bus) and the settings and the cable depths of the *other free modulators*; a lane's and a group's modulator do not reach it, nor it theirs. *What it hears.* Every note and every source: `Events::all()` is every message of the block whatever its source (it has no key range, remap or transpose, and belongs to no lane whose sources could be chosen), so that an envelope opens on any note, a retriggering LFO and a step sequencer start again on any, a velocity or a key control follows the last note that anyone plays and a MIDI control learns and follows from any source on any channel. *When it runs.* First in `process_events`, before the groups' modulators and before any lane renders: tick (with the tempo), `apply_cross_mod`, publish the outputs, tell the main thread of a control that has learned, then `apply_free_modulators`: the plugin of each cable is found by its node anywhere in the graph (`locate_anywhere`: a lane's chain by `slot_in_chain`, then a group's bus), the offsets of the cables on one parameter are **added** and the sum held to the parameter's range, and the parameter is set to the value the user set plus it. **The nearer to the plugin wins**: a group's modulator on the same parameter writes after it and a lane's own after that, each from the user's value and its own offsets, so a free modulator's offset is not added to theirs. A cable whose plugin is not in the graph drives nothing and publishes nothing. A session with none runs none of it (a check that the list is empty).
  - **The intents and the history.** `AddFreeModulator { kind }` (the kinds of `AddModulator`) puts a modulator at the end of the session's own rack: a step ("add an LFO": undone by `RemoveNode`, made again under its id), told as a snapshot. `AddModEdge` takes a free modulator as it takes any, and refuses what is out of its reach; `Modulate` still makes a lane's or a group's. `RemoveNode` of a free modulator takes out the cables that drive its settings and depths first, gives what its cables drove the value that the user set, and is put back whole by undo. **The cables of free modulators to a plugin go with the plugin**, written down for undo: `remove_effect`, `remove_bus_effect`, `put_instrument` and `clear_instrument` already took every cable to it (`cables_into_plugin` looks in every rack), and `remove_lane` and `remove_group` take those to the plugins of the lane and of the group's bus effects (`SessionModel::free_cables_into`); the free modulator stays.
  - **The file.** A top-level `[[modulator]]` with a lane modulator's keys, written after the `[[group]]` tables and before the `[[cable]]` ones, and `[[modulator.target]]` with `to = "instrument[0].effect[1]"` (the place of the plugin, as an audio cable names its ends: `CablePlace`) and `param`, or a sibling by `mod_rate`, `mod_attack`…, `mod_depth = [m, c]` as a lane's. The loader (`load_free_modulators`, after every lane and group, over `make_rack`, the tail that it now shares with the lane's loader and the group's) makes the nodes first, plans each cable (`plan_free_target`) and loads without one that drives nothing, with the reason in the log (a `to` that is missing, that is not a place of the session or names no plugin, a parameter that the plugin has not, a sibling that is not there, itself). The ids of a free modulator's nodes come after the group modulators' and before the sources', so that a session with none has the ids it had. A negative rate and the steps of a step sequencer are checked in a free modulator as anywhere (`modulator[1].rate is below 0 (-1): …`).
  - **The terminal.** The tree has the free modulators first, in magenta, each saying what its cables drive by the lane or the group of the plugin (`~ LFO 0.5Hz sine → L1 Oscillator: detune (30%), G1 Filter (bus): cutoff (40%), Mod 1 attack (25%)  (free)`); `F` adds a free LFO and puts the cursor on it (`m` on a free modulator adds another), `t` opens the target selector (every parameter of every plugin, each labelled by its lane or group, and the sibling free modulators' settings), `d` takes it out, its rows are edited as a lane modulator's, and `m` and `l` on a row of its pane cross-modulate or learn it; its action bar is `F new free`, `t add target`, `d delete`, and the Help tab lists `F`.
  - **The page.** The protocol has the intent (`Intent.ts`, generated), `toFlow` lays a modulator that has no parent out as a node of its own, and the mock engine refuses the intent (`the mock engine has no modulator that is in no lane yet`). A session that has free modulators, served by `tang serve`, is drawn by the page as it stands (looked at in a browser against the real program, with `examples/shared-lfo.toml`: the LFO is a node under the lanes with its rate, wave, retrigger and fade, its trace, and the two cables dashed to the cutoff knobs that they drive with the sliders of their depths, +20% and -20%; no error in the page or the program; not in a spec), but the page's rule of what a modulator can drive does not know one that has no parent (the list at the foot of the node says `Nothing to drive`: a cable cannot be drawn from it), and it has nothing to make one with and nothing in a knob's `~` menu to attach one: that is P5b-3.
  - **The oracle.** A session (`freemod`: a free LFO with cables to an oscillator's detune, a filter's cutoff and a reverb's damping on a bus, a free envelope with a cable to the filter's resonance and another to the LFO's rate, a free step sequencer on the second oscillator's detune) and a scenario (`edited:freemods`, 19 edits, every one made: modulators of three kinds made while a chord is held and cables drawn to every kind of plugin, the cutoff set by the user, the filter taken out while a free cable drives it and put back by Undo, a lane taken out with the sequencer's cable and put back, the LFO taken out and put back, the group taken out with the envelope's cables to its reverb and put back, taken out by Redo and put back again); `Edit::{AddFreeModulator, FreeCable, RemoveFreeModulator}`, `Scenario::has_free_modulators`, and the facts hold the engine's free rack to the model's after every block. The loop that the plan replaced does not tick free modulators, so a scenario that has any is not held to it (`is_in_the_old_loop`).
  - **The example.** `examples/shared-lfo.toml`: a saw and a square an octave above it, each through a low-pass filter, and one sine LFO of 0.5 Hz (a free modulator) with a cable of depth +0.2 to the saw's filter and one of -0.2 to the square's: the two take turns, two seconds a turn. It is the case that the step is for, and what a person can try now (`tang --web examples/shared-lfo.toml`: the terminal edits it, the page draws it and plays it with its keys, and so does a MIDI keyboard), since the page cannot make or aim a free modulator yet.
  - **The held things.** *The oracle:* 1005 renders held to the bit (the whole corpus in release, 5 tests with the benchmark and the WAV files, 99 s): the 999 that were there are the same bits and the six that are new are stored (6 lines in `exact/macos-aarch64.txt` and 2 in `fingerprints.txt`, additions only); 796 of the 900 generated renders are heard and 47 clip, and 1,769 of their 2,043 edits are applied, as before. *Rust:* 64 new tests, and one on the real program (below): the engine's 17 (what the free section writes: the parameters in any lane and on any bus, two free modulators on one parameter, the range that their sum is held to, two parameters of one plugin, a plugin that is nowhere; what wins: a group's modulator and a lane's on a parameter that a free one drives; what it hears: every note whatever the lanes' ranges and sources, and the tempo; a control that learns; cables among the free modulators and none to a lane's or a group's; what the user sets and what a cable is centred on; the commands of a rack and the facts; the published values), the model's 4 (the cables into a plugin and the free cables into those of a lane or a group, reach, nodes and ids, what goes with a plugin), the controller's 11 (the intent for every kind, a cable to any plugin and what is refused, cables to the settings of a sibling, `Modulate` for a setting, a free modulator taken out and what it drove, the cables that go with an effect, an instrument, a lane and a group), the loader's 8 (the nodes and the commands, the ids, the places of any lane and any group, a cable that names what is not there, the centres, the telemetry's slots, the file that a save writes and a load reads, a session with none), the session's 1, the graph's 3, the layout's 1, the oracle's 2, the terminal's 15 golden tests (the tree and its snapshot, `F`, the selector and its binding, the rows of the pane, the Type row, `d` and undo, the popup of cross-modulation, learning, what goes when a plugin goes, the scope, the second free modulator's pane and `d`) and the example's 2 in `audio.rs`; the intent's wire test, the history's lists of what is undone and the allocator's test have free modulators in them too. *The terminal:* 13 golden tests (the tree, `F`, the selector, its binding, the rows of the pane, the Type row, `d` and undo, the popup of cross-modulation, learning, what goes when a plugin goes, the scope) and one snapshot (`session_free_modulator`); the 356 older ones are unchanged. *The real program:* a test of `tests/serve.rs` drives a WebSocket client that makes a free modulator, draws a cable from it to a parameter, and saves, and a second program started on the saved file has them. *The web:* one test of `toFlow` for a modulator with no parent; lint and typecheck clean.
  - **Decisions I made, which you may overrule** (D91). That a free modulator **hears every note and every source**: it belongs to no lane, so no range or set of sources applies, and a cable of notes into a modulator is for later. That **the nearer to the plugin wins** (a lane's own modulator over a group's over a free one's: a lane's has always won over a group's) and that **two free modulators on one parameter add up**, as two of a lane's do. That a free modulator **reaches any plugin of the session and the settings of the other free modulators only**: the settings of a lane's or a group's modulator are those racks' own. That **the file names the plugin by its place** (`to = "instrument[0].effect[1]"`), as the audio cables name their ends, and not by a rack-relative slot, which a free cable has none of. That **`F`** adds one in the terminal (the plan had `m` with no lane selected; the cursor of the tree is always on something of a lane's, a group's or now a free modulator's, so it is a key of its own). That **a cable of a free modulator to a plugin goes with the plugin**, as every cable to it does, and is put back by undo. That **the mock engine refuses the intent** until the page can draw one (P5b-3), where the alternative was a mock that makes a free modulator that nothing draws. And that **P5b-2a came first**, as a refactor of ten pairs of commands into ten, held by the oracle before anything new was built on it.

  - **What it is.** A look-ahead peak limiter (`src/plugin/chain/limiter.rs`): the loudest sample of either channel (linked, so that the stereo image does not move) says what gain would bring a frame down to the ceiling; the sound is held back by the look-ahead (2 ms, 95 frames at 48 kHz) and each frame comes out with the least gain wanted over the frames from it to the look-ahead after it (a sliding minimum, so that the gain is down when a peak arrives), which goes up again by an exponential release of 80 ms and is averaged over the look-ahead (so that it comes down in a ramp and not a click). Every gain in the average is at most what its own frame wanted: **a frame never comes out over the ceiling**. The master node (`Master` in `nodes.rs`) turns the mix by the volume (a linear ramp over the block), puts it through the limiter (a switch is a crossfade over the block: the limited sound is a look-ahead later) and copies it to the output, **bit for bit as it always was when the volume is 1 and the limiter is out of the sound**; the meter and the scope read what comes out. The engine publishes how far the limiter works in a telemetry cell of its own, the last of the 4,096, which is never handed out. See "The master limiter and volume" in `CLAUDE.md` for the model, the file (`[master]`), the intents, the terminal and the page.

The whole of it, **a set of nodes with cables taken out of a session and loaded as one node of another graph**, needs the lane to be dissolved (P5c: a netlist, with the ports that a module shows) and a library of references (P6 of `docs/patch-graph.md` §11.6); what can be built now, on the lane as the model has it, with nothing to take back later, is the part that the page already draws: **a lane that only holds effects** is a row of free modules, and its chain is a thing that a person builds, tunes and wants again.
  - **What it is.** A **module is the chain of effects of one lane**: its effects in order, each as a session file says an effect (the plugin, the preset by its name, the values that are not the plugin's own once the preset is loaded, the mix, the knobs pinned to its node, whether the stage before it feeds it) and the audio cables that are between those effects (a second input included), and nothing else: no instrument, no modulator, no source of notes, no group, no place on the canvas, and no cable that goes into the chain or out of it (those are the person's, drawn once the module is in a session). It is **saved** by the new intent `SaveModule { node, name }` (`node` is a lane or an effect of its chain; told as `ModuleSaved { name }`), **listed** in the catalog as `module:<name>` with the plugins (format `Module`, no instrument, as many parameters as effects, no presets) and **added** by `AddFreeEffect { plugin: "module:<name>" }`, which makes a lane of its own, bare as every module that stands by itself is, with all the effects and the cables in it. A module is a **copy**: what is changed in its file later changes no session that has it.
  - **The file.** A session file of one lane that has no instrument (`app/module.rs`: `parse` refuses a file that has an instrument, a second lane, a group, a modulator of any kind, a source of notes, no effect or a cable that is not between two effects of the chain; `to_text` writes it, behind a comment line that says what it is, so that a person can read it, keep it in a repository and edit it by hand). It is the reader and the writer of sessions that read and write it, so a module is made of what a session is made of.
  - **The library.** A directory, `~/.config/tang/modules/` (`TANG_MODULES_DIR` says another: the tests of the real program and the browser specs each give a program a directory of its own), one file `<name>.toml` for each module, the name a plain file name (`module::clean_name`: the rule of Save as, without the extension, and not a name that ends in `.toml` twice, which the listing would give another name). The controller reads it when the program starts and again when a module is saved (`Controller::refresh_modules`); it does not watch it. A controller with no library (the tests') lists none and refuses to save one.

The Help tab lists both keys.

Step 104 had tied the sub-graph to P5c and to a library of references, and the picture is not that: the lane is only how the model holds a plugin, an effect that stands by itself is a lane that has no instrument, and a session file can hold any number of such lanes with cables between their plugins. What P5c and P6 make is a module as **one node with ports** in another graph and by reference; a module as **a copy of nodes with the cables between them** (as VCV Rack's "save selection" is) needs neither.
  - **What it is.** A module is **the plugins that are chosen** (the instrument of a lane, which is the lane's node, or an effect, from any lanes) **and the audio cables that have both ends among them**: each lane that has one of them is a lane of the module, with its instrument if it was chosen and the effects that were, in the order of their chains, each as it is now (the preset by its name, the values that are not the plugin's own, the mix of an effect and the volume of an instrument, the knobs pinned, whether the stage before an effect feeds it); what joins them to what is not chosen is left out: the cables that go in and out, the way out of a lane, the key range, the pattern, the mute and the solo. **A link from a stage that was not chosen is cut in the module** (`feed = "none"`): an effect that is the first of its lane in the module and was not the first in the session, or that follows one that was left out, is fed by the cables that are drawn and by nothing else. One step of the history: **`takes_out` is every lane that was made, the last first**, and a step's undo is a list (`Step::added`).

- [x] **106. A module holds the modulators that are chosen with its plugins (2026-10-30): an LFO on a filter that is in the module is saved with its cable and added again with it.** *Done when:*

Step 105 left a modulator that was chosen out of the module and counted it among what a module cannot hold; the cables that modulators have to the plugins that are chosen were not kept, nor was the ear. The modulators are the session's own since step 96 (a node with an ear and cables that name what they drive by the node), so that a module can hold them as it holds plugins, with nothing new in the model: a `[[modulator]]` in the module's file, each with the lane of the module that it hears and the cables that drive what is in the module.
  - **What it is.** A module is now the plugins that are chosen, the audio cables that have both ends among them **and the modulators that are chosen with them**: each as it is now (its kind and its settings: an LFO's waveform, rate, key and fade, an envelope's stages, a macro's value, a control's binding, a step sequencer's steps), **the lane of the module that it hears** if it heard a lane that is a lane of the module (otherwise every note: a group is never kept) and the cables **whose ends are in the module**: a parameter of a plugin that is chosen (by name), the volume of an instrument that is chosen and the mix of an effect that is chosen, a setting of another modulator that is chosen (a rate, a stage of an envelope), and the depth of another cable that is kept. What it drives that is not chosen is left out; **a cable that drives the depth of another goes with that other**, and the place that a cable has in the file is its rank among the cables of its modulator that stay. A modulator that is chosen and has no cable that stays is in the module all the same.
  - **The file.** The same session file: `[[modulator]]` tables with `hears = "instrument[N]"` (a lane of the module) and `[[modulator.target]]` tables (`to` and `param`, or `to` and `gain = "volume"` or `"mix"`, or `mod_rate`, `mod_attack`, `mod_decay`, `mod_sustain`, `mod_release`, or `mod_depth = [m, c]`). `app/module.rs` reads them (`ModuleModulator`, `ModuleTarget`, `ModuleDrives`: `Param`, `Gain`, `Setting`, `Depth`) with every place looked for among the module's own, as the audio cables' are: a `hears` that is not a lane of the module, a `to` that is not a plugin of it, a volume of an effect, a mix of an instrument, a modulator that is not there or is itself, a cable that the other has not and a cable that drives nothing refuse the file with the place; the writer (`modulators_of_text`) is `source_to_save`, which the session's saver uses too, behind a loop that takes out the cables that drive the depth of a cable that went until none more goes.
  - **The controller.** `SaveSelectionAsModule` takes modulators in `nodes`; a modulator alone is refused (`a modulator alone is not a module: choose the effects or instruments that it goes with`), and the refusals for a group, a bus effect and a source of notes are as they were. `AddFreeEffect` of a module makes the modulators after the lanes and their audio cables (`make_module_modulators`): all of them first, each hearing the lane of the module that it heard (`add_modulator_hearing`, which makes the node, the ear and the slots), then the cables that drive a parameter, a volume, a mix or a setting, in the order of the file (`module_cable` over `param_cable`, `gain_cable` and `field_cable`, as the intents make them, at the depth that the file says held to a depth's range), and then the cables to a depth, in sweeps, each as soon as the cable that it drives is made. What cannot be made (a parameter that the plugin has not, a value that a modulator drives already, a setting that the other has not) is logged and left out, with nothing allocated for it. **It is the same step of the history**: `takes_out` takes every lane and every modulator that was made out, the last first (the modulators were made last, so they go first), and a redo makes them again under the same ids.
  - **The terminal.** `N` adds a module that has modulators as it adds any, in one step that Ctrl+Z takes out whole; the tree lists the modulators under the lane that each hears. `K` (the chain of a lane) saves no modulators, and there is no way to choose a graph in the terminal (the page has it).
  - **The page.** `modulePluginsOf` holds the modulators that are chosen and `Held.plugins` counts the instruments and the effects; the bar's **Save as module…** is out of reach while no plugin is held (a modulator alone is not a module) and the status says why: `1 chosen, and a module needs an effect or an instrument`. Nothing in the session said that they had come together, so the page could not draw them as one thing. What was needed was a **record** of what one add made, and a way to draw the record as a single box.
  - **The record.** `ModuleInstance { node, name, members }` in `SessionModel::modules`: a node of its own (`NodePath::Module`, listed by `nodes()` after the modulators), the module's name in the library, and the lanes and the modulators that one add of it made (a lane's effects are in the lane). `AddFreeEffect { plugin: "module:<name>" }` makes it last, under a node that is allocated after everything else the add made, so that the ids of what the add made before it, and of every older fixture and oracle scenario, are what they were; no command goes to the audio thread, since the engine runs the plugins flat. A node is in at most one module, a member that is taken out leaves its module (written down as `Inverse::Module`, before the member's own inverse, so that Undo puts the member back first and the record after it) and a record with no member left is gone. `RemoveNode` of the node takes out **all that came with it as one step** ("remove Room": the record, then the members, the last made first), and is refused, with nothing changed and no step, when its lanes are all the lanes the session has. The box's ports are derived from the cables: the inputs of audio that nothing inside feeds, the outputs that nothing inside takes, an input of notes for each lane that takes notes, and every port that a cable crosses the edge at (`ModuleBox.tsx`: a row for each, `44 + rows × 28 + 20 + 16` pixels tall). A cable dragged to or from a box's handle is the cable to or from the node inside (`connection.ts` resolves the handle first), so the controller's rules judge it as they judge any cable. An open module has no box and a tag over its lanes, "▾ Room", that closes it; which modules are open is the viewer's own (`openModules.ts`, not saved, not sent, not in the history), and a module is closed when it is added.

## 13. Later: track B (`builtin:patch`)

A patchable synth that needs no host changes: a `builtin:patch` instrument that
holds its own voice graph (oscillator, filter, VCA, ADSR, LFO, mixer, …) with
typed cables (audio / control / gate). To the host it is just another `Plugin`,
so lanes, groups, modulators and the TUI are untouched. The graph is compiled on
the main thread into an immutable program and swapped on the audio thread
through the same send-in / return-old mechanism plugins use. It exposes macro
parameters to the host, so lane modulators and the TUI can drive it. The canvas
edits its inner graph, reusing the node / edge shapes from §4.2. Scope it after
the phase 0 tracer shows what the canvas wants; richer builtins (noise, VCA,
mixer, delay, …) are the natural first increment.

A proposal that grounds this in the engine as it is (what can be reused and what cannot, the one idea that keeps the controller and the page
almost as they are, the order of work, and the ten decisions that are the user's) is `docs/track-b.md`. Nothing of it is started.

### Sources as nodes (ideas)

Three ideas for after the canvas can build what the engine has now; none is started.

**A keyboard as a node.** Today every note goes to every lane (`NoteInput`: hardware MIDI, the virtual piano and the browser's keys are one
path) and each lane filters it by its own key range (`InstrumentLane.range`, `SetRange`). A keyboard node (the computer's keys, an on-screen
piano, a MIDI device) with a *MIDI cable* to a lane would take the range off the lane and put it on the keyboard, so that several keyboards
with ranges of their own (a split, a layer, one keyboard to two synths) are several nodes, and anything that sends notes can be a node as well:
a pattern, an arpeggiator, Web MIDI from the browser, a MIDI file. In the model it is a node kind and a port kind next to audio and modulation
(`NodeKind::Keyboard`, `Port::MidiOut` / `MidiIn`, `EdgeKind::Midi`); in the engine the global fan-out and range filter become a routing table
per lane (the channel-based routing of per-note expression stays as it is).

**Audio input as a source.** The engine has an output stream and no input. A lane whose chain starts at an input of the sound card (a
microphone, a line in) in place of an instrument would run through the same effects, groups, modulators and meters; an envelope follower is
the modulator that goes with it (what the input puts out, as an LFO's output is). From there, Tang as a plugin (VST3 or CLAP) whose buffer
comes from the DAW: `audio::Renderer` is already the one piece of code that the sound card's callback and the null backend run, so a plugin's
`process` would be a third thing that drives it, with the input as the source node's buffer.

*Built at step 99, as an instrument plugin in a lane that starts bare (`builtin:input`: see step 99 and D99), and not as the source node that this sketch has; what follows is what a node of its own would be, which P5c can make of it.* *Your ask of 2026-10-28, for after step 96 ("for future (after this) I want to be able to add my computer microphone as an input that I can connect to other devices via audio cable.")* turns it into the first thing to build of this idea, in the shape that the cables give it: the microphone is a **source node
with an output of audio**, as the keys and a MIDI device are sources of notes (P4), and what it puts out is drawn to what it is wanted at by an audio cable (an effect, a group's bus, the
mix), with the mute, the solo, the level and the latency that every cable has. A first sketch, nothing decided and nothing built: *the file* has a table for it (`[[input]]` with the device's
`name`, written as `[[device]]` is, and a `ui`), *the model* a node kind beside the sources of notes with a port `audioOut`, *the intents* `AddInput` (and its removal, with its cables, as a step of
the history) and `AddCable` from its output, *the controller* tells the audio thread the device it is to listen to, *the engine* opens an input stream on the device (cpal's, on its own callback)
and puts what it hears in a lock-free ring that the output callback reads a block at a time, so that the node in the plan is a source whose block is what the ring has (silence while it is empty,
and the null backend gives it silence or a test tone for CI), *the page* the bar's "+ Input" (the inputs that the program can open, as the open MIDI inputs are told: a message of its own) and
a node with an output port, *the terminal* a row for it on the Patch tab, and `tang enumerate audio` lists the inputs as well as the outputs. **Questions that are yours when it is started:**
which device the first one is (the system's default, or one that you choose, and whether a flag beside `--audio-device` names it); the permission that macOS asks of a program that opens a
microphone (the terminal that runs Tang is the one that is asked, once); the feedback of a microphone that is heard through the speakers that it listens to (it could begin muted, or at a low
level, or say so); a microphone is one channel and the chains are stereo (both sides get it); devices that do not run at the sample rate of the output (a resampler, or the same device only);
and the latency that the input adds, which the delay compensation of P3f already knows how to put in step with the paths that it is added to.

**Audio and MIDI as cables** (2026-10-20, yours). Every node has inputs and outputs, and the connections of audio and of MIDI are cables that a person
draws and takes out, as the modulation cables are: two oscillators into one reverb, a send, a bus into a bus, a keyboard (the computer's keys, a MIDI
device) with a cable to each lane it plays. It contains the two ideas above (a keyboard node is a MIDI source, an audio input is an audio source). What
the engine has and lacks, a staged path (audio cables first, as a routing table on the lanes and groups; then MIDI sources; then nodes between the keys
and the synth; a general engine only if it is still wanted) and the decisions that are yours are in `docs/patch-graph.md`. Nothing is started.

| # | Decision | Status |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Browser is a front-end to the same process; no audio in the browser; the TUI stays first-class | Agreed |
| D2 | v1 matches the Session and Piano tabs | Agreed |
| D3 | Track A (rack-as-patch on the existing engine) first; `builtin:patch` later | Agreed |
| D4 | Framework: robust, expandable, snappy → TypeScript + React + Vite + React Flow + Zustand, framework-agnostic client layer | Proposed (criteria agreed) |
| D5 | Controller is a plain struct driven by the owner loop; the web runtime talks to it by channels (no shared model, no locks) | Proposed |
| D6 | `axum` / `tokio` behind a `web` feature; Node in CI; assets embedded in the binary | Assumed |
| D7 | Graph-shaped wire model with stable `NodeId`s; layout stored in the session TOML as `ui` tables | Proposed |
| D8 | Telemetry via lock-free slots, binary frames; undo via inverse intents + recovered plugin instances | Telemetry built (step 6); undo of values built as D35, of what is added as D36, of what is taken out as D37 (cables, modulators, effects, lanes and groups, with the plugin instances, the lanes and the groups that the audio thread hands back) and of what is replaced (an instrument, with the plugin instance that the audio thread hands back, and a preset), also as D37 |
| D9 | Short design + TODOs in `CLAUDE.md`, long form here | Assumed |
| D10 | `tang serve` listens on `127.0.0.1:8765` by default; beyond loopback `--web-bind` and a token made for the run | Built (step 10) |
| D11 | One current-thread tokio runtime on its own thread for the server and the pusher; `ctrlc` for stopping a headless process | Built (step 10) |
| D12 | The client's store is vanilla zustand (no React in `client/`), the mock engine speaks the protocol through the same `Transport` as a socket, and the fixture the mock serves is generated from the Rust types and kept current by a Rust test | Built (step 11) |
| D13 | `web/dist` is embedded with `rust-embed`, with a committed `.gitkeep` so that the program builds without Node; the interface's content security policy has no `unsafe-*` | Built (step 11) |
| D14 | Telemetry never passes through React: one frame loop, readers that find their slot once for each layout, DOM writes only when a value moved; controls are controlled components, and what a control shows while the server catches up, and the one intent a frame, are the `Drive`'s | Built (step 12) |
| D15 | React Flow draws the canvas; `toFlow` is a pure function of the graph, nodes are functions of their data with controls that read their own values, and the canvas is laid out again only when the structure of the session changes (a function of the places it put the nodes at last too, from step 44: D45) | Built (step 12) |
| D16 | The TUI loop selects on a reader thread's channel, the browsers' requests and a tick, on the one controller; what the TUI changes without an intent is found by comparing what the subscribers were told with the session (`resync`, a snapshot at a revision of its own), until every edit is an intent | Built (step 13) |
| D17 | `--web[=ADDR]` is a flag of the TUI alone, with `serve`'s arguments (`127.0.0.1:8765`, `--web-origin`, a token beyond loopback); the address comes only after an `=`; the address and the warnings are printed before the TUI starts and shown in the tab bar and on the Help tab | Built (step 13) |
| D18 | The first of phase 3, a modulator's settings and a cable's depth, is done ahead of phase 1 (session parity): it is what the web UI is for ("build synths and control parameters with visual modulators"), it needs no structural intents, and it exercises the whole path (intent, controller, engine, event, reducer, control) on the thing the user wants to see | Built (step 14); say if phase 1 should have come first |
| D19 | What the client has to know about what the controller clamps to (the ranges of the gains, of a modulator's settings and of a cable's depth, what a new modulator starts as, the order of the waveforms) is generated into `web/src/protocol/generated/constants.ts` from the Rust that clamps, and checked by the test that checks the generated types; the client's mock engine and its controls read it and keep no copy | Built (step 14) |
| D20 | An intent that adds or takes out nodes or cables has no event a client could apply: `Applied.restructured` is set and the subscribers are given a snapshot at once, at the revision after the intent's, so that the controller's projection of the graph (the order of the nodes, the audio path, the layout of the telemetry) is the only one; the structural events of §5 are not built | Built (step 15) |

| D22 | Replacing a lane's instrument takes out every cable that drove the old plugin's parameters (a cable names its parameter by the plugin's own index, so one kept would drive whatever the new plugin has at that index); keeping the cables whose parameter the new plugin has under the same name is a later refinement, a TODO in `CLAUDE.md` | Built (step 20) |
